verdict: Avoid new unsecured electronics and mobile retail exposure in Delhi; lend only to established multi-brand chains with stock-and-receivable control and proven festive sell-through.
title: Delhi electronics & mobile retail: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Delhi electronics/mobile retailer buys handsets, accessories and appliances from OEMs and distributors, holds them in showroom and godown stock, and converts them to cash through counter sales, EMI/finance schemes and dealer credit.** Value sits in brand mix and footfall, not in the box; cash sits in inventory and receivables, and the cycle is short but unforgiving. Rating reports confirm the model is working-capital intensive by design, with inventory stocking and dealer credit driving high receivables [10], and TOL/TNW staying elevated to fund the book [9]. So when a proposal lands, check stock turns and receivable days first; if GCA days are rising, ask why before you look at the P&L. ## What has changed now
**Delhi is running behind the country: GST collections up 2.7% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand up 6.5% against 9.5% [D].** That is a local demand signal, not a national one, and it lands while repo sits at 5.5% with a tightening stance [D]. Peer results are strong but they are peers, not Delhi: SS Retail's Q1FY27 revenue grew 59% and PAT 61% YoY [4][6], and Electronics Mart's Q4FY26 PAT rose 49% with EBITDA up 20% [7]. Note SS Retail sells mainly in Tier II/III cities [4], so do not read its numbers as Delhi footfall. The Delhi Electronics Expo export-boom story is from March 2026 and is about exports, not local retail [2]; the DSIIDC electronics-city plan is from April 2025 and is policy intent, not demand [3]. ## Where the growth is
**Pursue established multi-brand chains and large-format showrooms with documented festive-season sell-through, and distributors tied to a single reputed OEM.** The Optiemus rating shows the distributor model works when anchored to Samsung/HTC-type brands [8], though that report is from December 2022 and must be refreshed. Avoid single-store dealers, pure online resellers and anyone whose growth is financed by unsold stock; the rating evidence is clear that slow-moving goods get liquidated through brand bank offers and price cuts [9], which hits margin, not just turnover. ## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending against stock and receivables, not clean limits.** Take monthly stock statements, ageing of inventory by SKU, and receivable ageing by dealer; covenant a maximum GCA-days level and a minimum stock turn. Collect from customer the current GCA days, inventory days and receivable days, since the rating data is dated. Price for the 5.5% repo [D] and keep tenor inside one festive cycle. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch stock ageing and dealer receivables monthly; a rise in either is the first sign of trouble.** If GCA days deteriorate the way Logica's did, from 84 to 96 days [10], cut limits and ask for brand-support confirmation. If EMI/finance rejections rise or footfall thins against the Delhi GST trend [D], treat it as demand, not collection, risk.
